page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. No marginal notes. Top: running head "IN IONAE CAP. IIII." with page number 401 at the top right. Bottom right: signature C and catchword "noftrae".

main_text.p: gorius Nazianzenus, & infinitis alij, ualde commouetur, cùm egregia doctrina, uirtute & auctoritate uiros, ex Ecclesiarum & Academiarum alueolis, ab inglorijs fu-cis hoc tempore pelli uider. Nec dubium est, hominem, qua parte adhuc animalis est, non posse non offendi tristissima specie Ecclesiae militantis, & fua uulnera deplorātis. Sed ut ἀθυμία [?] tandē, folis instar, in cordibus noftris exoriens, nebulas discutiat & tempestate sedet, recurrendum nobis est ad Deum, & firmiter statuendum, nihil temere fieri: Deum ex malis noftris bona facere: eundem efficere, ut omnia nobis adiumento sint in bonum: & mirando modo tenebras diuidere, sic ut in medijs malis ingentia bona, in summa (ut apparet) rerum confusione ἀντα-ξίαν [?] operum Dei, in oppresione & deformatione seruorum Dei liberatione, gloriam ueram & exaltationem, tandem aliquando animaduertamus.
Haec cum ita se habeant, ne intremus in iudicium cùm eo iudice, cui de mille interroganti ad unicum respondendo satisfacere non possumus. Adoremus eius iudicia & sanctam uoluntatem, & hanc noftrae

page.notes: Greek words ἀθυμία and ἀντα-ξίαν are doubtful; the Greek on the scan is small and the line breaks at "ἀντα-". The word "triftisima" was read as "tristissima" from the ligatures; the printed form is uncertain. The first word "gorius" is a fragment from the previous page (initial letter cut off). Page-number and running head read from the top line.
